newsitem.title: USA: US spot resids steady to up, aided by weather, gas.
newsitem.headline: US spot resids steady to up, aided by weather, gas.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices were unchanged to higher again Tuesday, underpinned by strong East Coast city gate gas prices amid the region's first cold snap, industry sources said.

"The demand is not huge because the cold weather just started, but we are seeing some interest from East Coast utilities," said one cash trader, noting resid has become more competitive with gas recently.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was unchanged at $19.50-75 a barrel, with November paper up slightly at $20.15-40 and December paper steady at $20.85-21.10.
NYH January one percent paper was little changed at about $21.50, traders said.
High sulphurs in NYH again edged up slightly on firmer bunkers, with 2.2 percent now talked on either side of $19.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices were stable, with one percent still at $17.75-$18.00 and three percent at $16.50-75.
USG December three percent paper held steady in the mid-$17 area, traders said.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York City gate swing gas prices jumped another 15 cents on the cold to about $3.45/mmBtu versus one percent resid at a $3.12/mmBtu equivalent. December gas in New York was still talked in the $3.90s/mmBtu compared to NYH December one percent resid paper at a $3.33/mmBtu equivalent.
